doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Leaving Toronto for Detroit and hearing Fletcher Henderson with Lester Young
summary: Debutante in Toronto, she goes to Detroit and the Graystone Ballroom, expecting Hawk and finding Lester in Henderson's band; then decides on Chicago.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: And when was the first time you got to see and hear jazz — to see something live?

You must stop me you know, if you want me to move from period to period — but because I would not do the things — my sister and I were close in age and we were debutantes in Toronto and that was Toronto for you. And she went on from there and had quite a wonderful career. And I said no, I’m going to the States. And my family didn’t think much of that. And so my mother said, “All right, I’ll take you to Detroit, and I’ll see that you’re set up properly, have a piano and somebody to watch over you” and so on. So I was in Detroit. So I said, “Okay, the Graystone Ballroom for me.” And it was Fletcher Henderson. And you know it was way back in ‘33 wouldn’t it be? Something like that. Stanley will correct me if I’m wrong. But anyway so for my long dream, for our deb party, I had wanted to have McKinney’s Cotton Pickers, because of Fats, who sang “Baby Won’t You Please Come Home,” and those wonderful things. And Fats died on the way up to Toronto. And so we never did get them. But Fletcher Henderson was a very good substitute as far as I was concerned, because I thought, at last Hawk. And so I arrived all alone, at the Graystone Ballroom in the black section of Detroit, and, all big guys, and making my way into the front of the bandstand, which is where I remained for the rest of my career. And there was Fletcher’s band, and where was Hawk? He’d just gone to England. And it was Lester. Well but you see I didn’t have enough ears, because I was listening for Hawk, and like the rest of the band, we all thought that Lester wasn’t making it, including Ms. Lee, Fletcher’s wife, who told him — you know Lester always tells, “Took him down in the basement” and said, “now listen to this, this is how you’re supposed to sound,” and you know enough to know what Prez was like, you know, such a gentle soul. He wouldn’t say to you you were all wrong or you aren’t with this or anything. But he soon quit the band. He wasn’t fired. They didn’t think he was doing a great job because he didn’t take Hawk’s place. But Lester knew, he went back to Basie. He went back to Kansas City. So well that was my first experience. And after that I quickly thought Detroit’s nowhere, and I must go to Chicago. And I was very lucky there, because I don’t know whether you know or not, did you ever hear of a man called Squirrel Ashcraft?
